LESSON: OPPORTUNITY IDENTIFICATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Social Entrepreneurship
Topic 4.2: Opportunity Identification
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Opportunity Identification, part of Social Entrepreneurship in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can you identify social enterprise opportunities in the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Opportunity Identification together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: Learners speak clearly and engagingly as they critique the different social

enterprise opportunities presented.

41

Values:
Unity: Learner collaborates with others to observe and interview the community to identify the resources available for

the social enterprise opportunity.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Civic responsibility: Learner engages in civic responsibility when prioritising and selecting the viable social enterprise

opportunity for adoption with the community.

Suggested learning resources:

Braille reference materials, print reference materials with appropriate font and colour contrast, print and braille

learner’s books, braille and print writing materials.
